inclusionReview.note: Tsushima (27–28 May 1905) is included as an individually reviewed naval battle. JACAR identifies the encounter between the Japanese and Russian fleets in the Tsushima Strait and surrounding waters. Its source item is classified as naval warfare, outside the automatic engagement-class discovery; this inclusion does not admit other instances of that broad class. The inherited event coordinate is a source locator, not the extent of the two-day action or reconstructed fleet positions.

note: Partial quantitative review of the 27–28 May 1905 battle. The comparable cohorts are the two initial main battle lines, twelve ships each, not the complete opposing fleets or equal fighting power. Other cruiser formations, torpedo craft and accompanying ships are explicitly unquantified; the main-line losses cannot be applied to them. Russia’s twelve main-line removals comprise eight sunk/scuttled ships and four captures. The two non-renderable breakdown observations are already included in twelve and must not be added again. No human deaths are inferred. The Japanese three-torpedo-boat loss and later fates of excluded Russian ships do not alter the main-line denominator. Pre-dreadnought models represent the battleship components, not every armoured cruiser or coastal battleship; protected-cruiser models for the unquantified complements represent named cruiser components only, not torpedo craft or transports. The sources differ in complete-fleet scope, so no complete-fleet ratio is asserted. Tsushima (27–28 May 1905) is included as an individually reviewed naval battle. JACAR identifies the encounter between the Japanese and Russian fleets in the Tsushima Strait and surrounding waters. Its source item is classified as naval warfare, outside the automatic engagement-class discovery; this inclusion does not admit other instances of that broad class. The inherited event coordinate is a source locator, not the extent of the two-day action or reconstructed fleet positions.
